conversation.content: Let's start a deployment setup for the checkout service.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment", "value": {"name": "checkout-service"}}]
Run four copies of it to start.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/replicas", "value": 4}]
Give each copy half a CPU core to work with.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/resources/requests/perPodCpu", "value": "500m"}]
Allocate 768 MiB of memory to each copy.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/resources/requests/perPodMemory", "value": "768Mi"}]
Also show the combined CPU request for the whole rollout and how it’s calculated.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/resources/requests/totalCpu", "value": {"value": "2000m", "formula": "replicas * perPodCpu = 4 * 500m"}}]
Do the same for the combined memory request.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/resources/requests/totalMemory", "value": {"value": "3072Mi", "formula": "replicas * perPodMemory = 4 * 768Mi"}}]
Add a quick note that summarizes how many running copies this setup provides, including the calculation.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/capacitySummary", "value": {"value": 4, "formula": "replicas = 4"}}]
During voluntary disruptions, require one fewer than the full set to stay running, and include the math.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/availability/disruptionBudget/minAvailable", "value": {"value": 3, "formula": "replicas - 1 = 4 - 1"}}]
Also cap voluntary disruptions at one unavailable copy, with the calculation made explicit.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/availability/disruptionBudget/maxUnavailable", "value": {"value": 1, "formula": "constant 1"}}]
Use the checkout container from our registry, pinned to the April release, and pull it only when needed.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/container/image", "value": {"repository": "registry.example.com/payments/checkout", "tag": "2026.04.3", "pullPolicy": "IfNotPresent"}}]
Expose the app’s HTTP traffic on port 8080.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/container/ports", "value": [{"name": "http", "containerPort": 8080, "protocol": "TCP"}]}]
Set it to run in production mode.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/container/env", "value": [{"name": "APP_ENV", "value": "production"}]}]
Point it at the internal payment API endpoint.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/container/env/-", "value": {"name": "PAYMENT_API_URL", "value": "https://payments.internal.svc.cluster.local"}}]
Have it wait up to five seconds when calling upstream services.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/container/env/-", "value": {"name": "UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS", "value": "5000"}}]
Add a readiness check on the app port at /ready, starting after ten seconds.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/probes/readiness", "value": {"path": "/ready", "port": 8080, "initialDelaySeconds": 10}}]
Add a liveness check on /healthz using the same app port, but let it start after thirty seconds.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/probes/liveness", "value": {"path": "/healthz", "port": 8080, "initialDelaySeconds": 30}}]
Make it reachable inside the cluster on port 80, forwarding traffic to the app port.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/service", "value": {"type": "ClusterIP", "port": 80, "targetPort": 8080}}]
Put it in the payments namespace and label it for the checkout app.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/metadata", "value": {"namespace": "payments", "labels": {"app": "checkout"}}}]
Add ownership details so the platform team knows who supports it and which cost center to charge.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/metadata/annotations", "value": {"owner": "payments-platform", "supportChannel": "#payments-oncall", "costCenter": "fintech-042"}}]
Make sure it matches the checkout workload using the app and frontend tier labels.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/selector", "value": {"matchLabels": {"app": "checkout", "tier": "frontend"}}}]
Roll out updates gradually, allowing a small surge but no planned downtime.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/strategy", "value": {"type": "RollingUpdate", "maxSurge": 1, "maxUnavailable": 0}}]
Run the workload as a non-root user and avoid privilege escalation.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/securityContext", "value": {"runAsNonRoot": true, "runAsUser": 10001, "allowPrivilegeEscalation": false}}]
Set sensible upper bounds so a single copy can’t consume too much CPU or memory.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/resources/limits", "value": {"perPodCpu": "1000m", "perPodMemory": "1Gi"}}]
Schedule it onto the general-purpose Linux worker pool in the primary zone.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/scheduling/nodeSelector", "value": {"kubernetes.io/os": "linux", "nodepool": "general-purpose", "topology.kubernetes.io/zone": "us-east-1a"}}]
Allow it to run on nodes reserved for payment workloads.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/scheduling/tolerations", "value": [{"key": "workload", "operator": "Equal", "value": "payments"}]}]
Prefer spreading it across hosts so a single machine issue doesn’t take out multiple copies.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/scheduling/podAntiAffinity", "value": {"topologyKey": "kubernetes.io/hostname", "labelSelectorApp": "checkout", "weight": 80}}]
Mount the shared config file into the container without allowing writes.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/volumes", "value": [{"name": "checkout-config", "configMap": "checkout-config-v3", "readOnly": true}]}]
Place that configuration under /etc/checkout inside the app.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/container/volumeMounts", "value": [{"name": "checkout-config", "mountPath": "/etc/checkout", "readOnly": true}]}]
Add a secret for the payment gateway token and keep it mounted read-only.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/volumes/-", "value": {"name": "gateway-token", "secret": "payment-gateway-token", "readOnly": true}}]
Mount that token under /var/run/secrets/payments in the container.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/container/volumeMounts/-", "value": {"name": "gateway-token", "mountPath": "/var/run/secrets/payments", "readOnly": true}}]
Send application logs in structured format at info level, with request identifiers included.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/observability/logging", "value": {"format": "json", "level": "info", "includeRequestId": true}}]
Scrape metrics from the app on the usual Prometheus path every half minute.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/observability/metrics", "value": {"enabled": true, "path": "/metrics", "intervalSeconds": 30}}]
Turn on tracing and sample one out of ten requests.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/observability/tracing", "value": {"enabled": true, "sampleRate": 0.1}}]
Send traces to the in-cluster collector using OTLP.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/observability/tracing/exporter", "value": {"endpoint": "http://otel-collector.observability.svc:4317", "protocol": "otlp"}}]
Make it available through the internal ingress at checkout.payments.example.com using TLS.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/ingress", "value": {"className": "internal-nginx", "host": "checkout.payments.example.com", "tlsEnabled": true}}]
Use the managed certificate for that hostname and route only the root path.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/ingress/tlsSecretName", "value": "checkout-payments-tls"}, {"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/ingress/path", "value": "/"}]
Only allow inbound traffic from the ingress controller and the frontend namespace.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/networkPolicy/ingress", "value": {"allowedFromNamespace": "frontend", "allowedFromApp": "internal-nginx", "policyType": "Ingress"}}]
For outbound traffic, let it reach DNS and the payments API.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/networkPolicy/egress", "value": {"allowDns": true, "allowPaymentsApi": true}}]
Use the standard service account with token mounting turned off, and don’t create a new one for this.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/serviceAccount", "value": {"name": "checkout-runtime", "automountToken": false, "create": false}}]
Keep old rollout history for ten releases and give new copies a minute to shut down cleanly.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/lifecycle", "value": {"revisionHistoryLimit": 10, "terminationGracePeriodSeconds": 60, "progressDeadlineSeconds": 600}}]
Finish it with basic alert routing for the on-call team, including the severity and runbook link.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/alerts", "value": {"route": "payments-oncall", "severity": "warning", "runbookUrl": "https://runbooks.example.com/payments/checkout"}}]

edit_instruction: Update it to run 6 copies of the checkout service.
conversation_pattern: Center the artifact on a deployment with a replica count, per-pod CPU and memory requests, and availability settings, where EVERY derived field carries its own explicit formula written in the artifact: total CPU = replicas * perPodCpu, total memory = replicas * perPodMem, capacity summary = replicas, and each disruption-budget value has a stated formula (e.g. minAvailable = replicas - 1, maxUnavailable = 1). Do not include any availability field whose dependence on the replica count is not given by a stated formula. Around this core, add the realistic, independent details a deployment config would carry that do not depend on the replica count, and vary their number from sample to sample.
edit_pattern: Change the replica count to a specific new number.
cascade_pattern: Editing the replica count re-derives total CPU, total memory, capacity summary, and each disruption-budget value strictly from its stated per-pod value and formula. Per-pod requests and unrelated deployment fields stay unchanged.
annotation_notes: replicas 4->6; totalCpu=6*500=3000m, totalMemory=6*768=4608Mi, capacity=6, minAvailable=6-1=5. maxUnavailable constant 1 unchanged. formula-text fields embed the old count -> optional (updating or leaving both acceptable).
